status.en: 123 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 123 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Militant attacks continue across Nigeria, with suspected militants killing at least 30 people in Niger state and gunmen killing 16 in a midnight raid on Bassa community in Plateau. Bandits abducted six people in Kaduna and six in Chikun LGA, while gunmen opened fire on Peter Obi’s rally in Edo, injuring one person. President Tinubu vowed to rescue abducted schoolchildren in Borno and ordered an onslaught against terrorists. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Militantangrep fortsetter over hele Nigeria, med mistenkte militante som drepte minst 30 personer i Niger-staten og væpnede som drepte 16 i et midnattangrep på Bassa-samfunnet i Plateau. Banditter bortførte seks personer i Kaduna og seks i Chikun LGA, mens væpnede åpnet ild mot Peter Obis møte i Edo og såret én person. President Tinubu lovet å redde bortførte skolebarn i Borno og beordret en offensiv mot terrorister. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
